functionalObligations.text: a venue is chosen for the user across third-party liquidity providers on CeFi and DeFi exchanges; the user names no venue and is shown only the result
functionalObligations.note: Ag is asserted on the operator's own wording. The venue set, the algorithm, the provider identities and the route are all unpublished, so unlike KyberSwap this Ag is discharged on assertion rather than on an inspectable mechanism. There is no repository for the routing engine and none for the router contract.

functionalObligations.text: the user is shown a single recommended provider rather than a route, and the rule by which that provider was chosen is not stated
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. This is discretion, not an auction and not a route. No symbol names administrative allocation of a fill without a stated rule. Ag names the construction of a route; it does not name the unexplained selection of a counterparty.

functionalObligations.text: whether any counterparty ever signs a firm quote that this system then fills is not stated at any primary source; the published wording ('CeFi and DeFi exchanges') is equally consistent with routing into an exchange-operated on-chain pool
functionalObligations.note: UNKNOWN, recorded as residue. DEPARTURE FROM THE CORPUS: the corpus decomposes Binance Wallet as {Ag, Rf} with a marker saying Rf is 'partly INFERRED'. Stage 1 searched and found no primary evidence for RFQ at all, and there is no repository and no developer documentation to check against. Rf is therefore DROPPED from the construction rather than carried with a marker, per the standing rule that a finding of failure beats a forced fit.

functionalObligations.text: the user sets a slippage tolerance beside a displayed Minimum Received, and bears every adverse move between signature and inclusion; all swaps are final once confirmed
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, the same gap as LiquidMesh F4. No element names a settlement-enforced output floor on a swap the user executes for themselves; In presumes a filler distinct from the signer, and there is none.

functionalObligations.text: the user pays network gas on every swap, including on swaps that fail, and no fee sponsorship is offered at any point
functionalObligations.note: DEPARTURE FROM THE CORPUS. The corpus carries a CANDIDATE-REGISTER marker for Gs (sponsored-fee liability) on Binance Wallet and a residue line about gasless swap UX. The primary announcement says the opposite in terms: 'users will still need to pay for network gas fees'. Gs is unwarranted and is not carried. Recorded as an obligation so the negative is on the record rather than merely absent.

functionalObligations.text: the user's transactions are shielded from the public mempool by default, by a private-RPC programme operated by the host chain and its partners rather than by this application
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Two gaps at once: no element names a transaction's path to inclusion, and no element can express that a protocol's stated property is inherited from its host chain's infrastructure rather than produced by the protocol. The wallet consumes an ecosystem service here; it does not operate one.

functionalObligations.text: settlement runs through a router the operator built and controls, deployed at a single vanity address across seven EVM chains and as a matching-prefix program on Solana, implemented as an EIP-2535 Diamond whose facets a single owner address may replace selector by selector
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE, and a departure from the corpus {Ag, Rf}. Up names a mutable implementation proxy; it does not name per-selector facet replacement, in which parts of the contract can be swapped independently. Owner is an EOA (0xEe7b429Ea01F76102f053213463D4e95D5D24AE8) with no timelock published, so X9 (Up with immediate single-key control) is armed and L15 (Up implies Tg or a bounded emergency process) is not discharged.

functionalObligations.text: the settlement contract's bytecode is verified against a source blob the operator uploaded to a block explorer, while no public, versioned or reviewable codebase for it exists anywhere
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. No element expresses the evidentiary status of the code that implements the mechanism. 'Verified' here means the bytecode matches an uploaded blob, not that it matches a public codebase, and a decomposition cannot tell the two apart.

functionalObligations.text: the wallet holds the user's signing key as three MPC shares rather than as a single secret, so the party that routes the trade is also a party to producing the signature
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. The 58 contain no symbol for custody or key management of any kind. This gap recurs at Jupiter F14 (a custodial vault holding resting orders) and is worth escalating beyond this category.

functionalObligations.text: the swap sits inside an application that already holds the user's KYC-verified exchange account and balances, so the party that owns the demand also chooses the venue, and no consideration for that choice is disclosed in either direction
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the central one. Order-flow ownership stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief. This is the purest order-flow owner in the lane: it owns the exchange account, the wallet, the router, the chain on which 98.3 percent of its volume settles, and the token universe the user can see. There is no public evidence of payment for order flow and equally none of its absence; unlike OKX no conflict-of-interest policy is published. The vocabulary spends four symbols on how an order is matched and none on who was entitled to decide where it went.

functionalObligations.text: the right to fill is not auctioned, not tendered and not priced: there is no solver set, no bidding, no eligibility rule and no published list of the providers that supply the other side
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, recorded as a null. Solver eligibility stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief. Whether the operator or an affiliate is ever the maker is UNKNOWN and no primary source addresses it.

functionalObligations.text: the application claims to find the most competitive price from thousands of options on CeFi and DeFi exchanges, with no benchmark named, no measurement published and no disclosure of the alternatives that were rejected
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Price-improvement benchmarking stated as its own obligation per the stage-2 brief. X14's second limb (a price-improvement claim with no named benchmark) holds squarely; its first limb (exclusive market structure) is UNKNOWN, because the provider set is unpublished and therefore cannot be shown either exclusive or open.

functionalObligations.text: trading fees on all swaps were waived for eight months, scoped to particular products and to backed-up keyless addresses only, with imported wallets excluded
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Nothing names a temporary, conditional, product-scoped and wallet-type-scoped price of zero, which is a distribution instrument rather than a fee schedule. The CURRENT STANDING SWAP FEE IS UNKNOWN: no primary source states it, and the figures circulating on review sites are not carried, per invariant 5.

functionalObligations.text: limit orders placed in the Alpha product execute against on-chain markets and their fee was cut from 0.15 percent to 0.01 percent on one chain
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Ob was considered and is NOT asserted: no primary source establishes whether a book exists on-chain, off-chain, or at all, so the mechanism is UNKNOWN and only the fee change is citable.

functionalObligations.text: an exchange Spot or Funding balance can be turned into an on-chain trade with no wallet in the loop, and the order is auto-cancelled if the minimum received falls below the amount displayed
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. The custody boundary is crossed inside the mechanism: custodied exchange funds originate an on-chain swap. No element names origination of an on-chain trade from an off-chain custodial balance.

functionalObligations.text: a token bought this way cannot be withdrawn or transferred out of the operator's environment until the operator lists it on its own exchange
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Fz (freeze / forced transfer, candidate) is the nearest and is rejected: the BEP-20 token itself is not frozen and carries no transfer restriction; the constraint is on the venue's withdrawal function, imposed by the same party that chose the venue. L28 would require a named authority, enumerated triggers, an appeal path and holder disclosure; none is present. Different actor, different object.

functionalObligations.text: the Alpha product is a region-gated and compliance-gated beta available only to accounts the operator deems eligible
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE, and a departure from the corpus {Ag, Rf}. Aw is an on-chain permission gate; this one is off-chain, applied at the product surface by the operator, and unenforced by the router, which anyone may call. Used per the standing principle of this lane: Aw for gates on the party seeking service, never for gates on who may fill.

functionalObligations.text: the operator disclaims being the counterparty and disclaims responsibility for the third-party applications into which it routes the user's trade
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. A routing system that selects venues while assuming no responsibility for them. Ag names the selection and is silent about who bears the consequence of it, which is precisely the commercial fact.

functionalObligations.text: the same router is deployed independently on twelve chains; no value crosses a domain and no message is verified between domains
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and a deliberate negative for stage 3: Xf and Xm are NOT discharged. 98.3 percent of volume settles on one chain, which the vocabulary also cannot express.

paper.title: Binance Wallet
paper.label: cat:int:binance
paper.blurb: A wallet front-end that routes its users' orders, with no public repository anywhere and no primary source for the quote mechanism the element-set decomposition assigns it. Its position in the category is owed to the order flow it originates rather than to any mechanism it operates.
paper.witnessReason: The witness drops both the quote element and the sponsored-fee element the element-set decomposition carries, because no primary source supports either and the gasless claim is contradicted by the venue's own documentation. Dropping an unsupported element is the same discipline as adding a supported one; here it leaves the construction very thin, and that thinness is the evidence.
paper.residueNote: This venue's entire economic position is that it owns the flow. The vocabulary has four symbols for how an order is matched and none for who owns it, so the thing that makes this a top-five venue is the thing the model cannot see.
